description: Adds one more delay tap to a Sapphire Echo chain, and goes to the right of Echo or of another Echo Tap

params.text: Adds another Echo Tap to the right, cloned from this tap's settings; pressed on the last tap of a chain that has no Echo Out, it inserts an Echo Out instead
Sets the delay time of this tap, from 0.1 seconds to 10 seconds; right-clicking it chooses whether this tap runs free or follows the clock on Echo
Attenuates and inverts the delay time CV
Places this tap in the stereo field; panning happens after the feedback path, so it moves where this tap lands without changing what flows to the next tap
Attenuates and inverts the panning CV
Places the send and return before the delay, so processed audio flows on through the chain, or after it, so processed audio stays local to this tap
Removes this tap from the chain, shifting the modules to the right back to close the gap
Sets the volume of this tap, outside the feedback path, so it changes the tap's loudness without changing the audio flowing through the chain
Attenuates and inverts the level CV
Reverses playback of this tap; with a gate patched to the reverse input, pressing it inverts the sense of that gate. Clicking the REV label switches to FLP, which reverses inside the feedback path
Sets the gain of this tap's envelope follower output
Resets this tap to its default settings, leaving the other taps alone
Silences every tap in the chain except this one

inputs.text: Scaled a volt per octave: each positive volt halves this tap's delay time and each negative volt doubles it
Moves this tap's position in the stereo field
Varies the volume of this tap
Left audio returning into this tap; patching this port breaks the internal short from the send ports on both the left and the right side
Right audio returning into this tap
In gate mode a high level reverses this tap; in trigger mode each pulse toggles it. The symbol above the REV label is clicked to change between the two modes

outputs.text: Left audio leaving this tap for outboard processing; it carries valid audio whether or not the return ports are patched
Right audio leaving this tap for outboard processing
Follows the amplitude of this tap, clamped to 0-10V through a bicubic limiter. Clicking the ENV label switches to DCK, where the voltage is 10V minus the envelope

notes: holding Shift while adding a tap gives the new tap default settings, and holding Command gives it a level of zero
this expander has no effect by itself: place it to the right of an Echo or of another Echo Tap, and it becomes one more tap of that chain.
menu: Polyphonic envelope output — switches this tap's envelope follower between one channel and one per audio channel; it is on the panel menu and on the envelope output port's own menu
Reverse/flip input port mode — chooses Gate or Trigger for the reverse input; it is on the panel menu and on the reverse input port's own menu
Time mode — chooses Seconds or Clock sync for this tap, and is on the TIME knob's own menu rather than the panel menu
Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero

inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±5V.
inputs.3:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±5V.
inputs.5:
continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the left return input.
inputs.6:
high above 1V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the REV button.
